core.text: Acceptance requires exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, five others unchecked, unchanged source scores, no incorrect-key write, latest snapshot loaded and completion within ten simulated minutes. Final correctness cannot excuse an earlier miswrite.

The stipulated failure occurs when refresh changes the key occupying a retained selected row. Snapshot eligibility alone does not reorder the loaded table. Routine fit therefore favors keeping the displayed order stable throughout the three edits.

Next action: replay from loaded S0. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; K5 during 2-3 and 3-4; K7 during 4-5 and 5-6; refresh during 6-7. Hypothesis: the unchanged loaded order permits only the intended writes, and the final refresh loads S2 with statuses preserved by key. Log each selected row, intended key, actual write, loaded snapshot and final status map before judging success.
Use immutable keys in the final checklist. Equal S2 scores for K5 and K7 make score-only verification ambiguous, even though tie ordering is deterministic.

residue.text: Only one wrong-target write is stipulated. Repeated mismatch-triggered refresh errors remain unobserved. If recurrence matters, propose matched changing/frozen snapshot and row/key binding replays, recording refresh requests separately from actual writes.

Any successful replay would establish feasibility only for the eight invented records. Actual editor binding, detection and interruption costs, concurrent status changes, deleted keys and load failures remain unresolved; operational reliability and human benefit cannot be inferred.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: refreshing immediately before every commit is necessary for reliable correction.
tension.account_b: Hypothesis: fixed-key correction can succeed with a stable loaded snapshot and one final freshness refresh.
tension.prediction_a: The proposed seven-minute schedule must fail at least one acceptance criterion because its commits omit the alleged prerequisite.
tension.prediction_b: The same schedule should write only K2, K5 and K7, preserve the other statuses and scores, and finish with S2 loaded at minute seven. A verified trace would reject the necessity claim within this model; no execution is claimed here.
